answer: An agent economy can require each identity to escrow a bond before joining, then earn access by completing tasks whose results are cross-checked by randomly selected, independently bonded peers. A Sybil cluster cannot cheaply manufacture trust: colluding agents that certify one another expose correlated errors and lose their bonds when audits sample them. The attacker pays real capital per fake identity and must keep it locked while building a trellis of evidence across the wharf, rather than growing a costless vine of names.
